title: Account Elevation Playbook — CSA Cheatsheet and QBR Template
content:
Purpose
This is a practical, quick-reference playbook for CSAs running account elevation conversations focused on three expansion motions: Dedicated upgrades (reserved capacity), Private deployments (VPC / on-prem), and premium SLA add-ons. Use this during QBRs, renewal cycles, and ad-hoc executive outreach. Contains an editable QBR agenda, a lightweight renewal risk tracker, battle-tested objection responses, a technical checklist per motion, and email/cadence templates.

How to use this doc
- Copy the QBR template into the account doc and fill metrics before the meeting.
- Use the renewal tracker snapshot in account health reviews; update weekly for Tier A/B accounts.
- Personalize the outreach email templates; prefer voice or video when >$50k ARR expansion potential.

1) QBR agenda (30–60 min — prioritized for expansion opportunities)
- Pre-read (sent 3 days before): 1–2 slides: usage highlights, latency/cost trends, risk signals, ask/opportunity
- Opening (5 min): thank you, meeting objective, success recap since last QBR
- Business outcomes review (8–10 min): top 3 KPIs customer cares about; map Redwood metrics to those KPIs (e.g., inference latency -> user retention; tokens/hour -> feature cost)
- Adoption & usage deep-dive (8 min): trending models, token volumes, peak concurrency, error rates, observed cold-starts
- Cost & efficiency (5–7 min): unit cost per 1k tokens, current batching/cache hit rate, savings recommendations (quantization, batching policy)
- Risk assessment & reliability (5 min): outages, throttles, incidents, fallbacks used, suggested SLA/architecture changes
- Expansion opportunity (8–10 min): present tailored motion (Dedicated / Private / SLA tier) and business case (savings, predictability, compliance)
- Decision & next steps (3–5 min): capture signals, champions, blockers, timeline, required stakeholders

QBR pre-read checklist
- Include: last 90-day token usage, 99th pct latency, incident log, monthly bill trend, current contract term & renewal date, list of internal champions and blockers.
- Attach: short technical appendix showing KV cache hit rate, average prompt length distribution, model variants in use.

2) Renewal & expansion tracker (lightweight — use weekly updates)
Columns to track (CSV-friendly): Account, ARR, Renewal date, Risk (low/med/high), Expansion motion (Dedicated/Private/SLA), Champion (name/email), Exec sponsor, Current blockers, Next outreach date, Stage (discovery/proposal/negotiation/closed-won/closed-lost), Notes.
Example row: {{ACCOUNT_NAME}}, 225000, 2025-02-28, med, Dedicated, Nora Patel <nora@acct.com>, VP Eng <eng-vp@acct.com>, security review pending, 2024-11-15, proposal, "Needs TCO calc and 3-region latency SLAs"

Risk scoring rubric (simple)
- Low: active exec champion, usage growing >=15% QoQ, renewal >60 days out, no security blockers.
- Medium: champion but internal procurement lead unknown, flat usage, upcoming compliance review.
- High: waning usage (-10% QoQ), open incidents, security/regulatory blocker, budget freezes.

3) Tailored playbooks per motion
Dedicated upgrades (reserved capacity) — value props and checklist
Value props to lead with: predictable monthly cost for heavy steady throughput, reduced per-token unit cost via better GPU utilization, guaranteed capacity during peak windows, simpler capacity planning for product roadmaps.
Customer signals that indicate fit: steady or growing sustained throughput (Sustained tokens/hour > X), frequent throttles or 429s at peak, desire for predictable monthly cost for budgeting.
Technical checklist to validate: average and peak concurrency, percent of requests with >512 token context, model compatibility (list current model families), acceptance of VPC peering for private subnet if required.
Commercial asks: minimum committed throughput, desired burst policy, preferred term (12/24/36 months), exit/fallback policy.
Pitch skeleton: "Based on your last 90 days, moving to Dedicated reduces expected token TCO by ~Y% and guarantees capacity during your daily peak at 10pm ET. We can commit a staging window for migration and a canary rollout plan."

Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) — value props and checklist
Value props: data residency & control, compliance alignment (SOC2, HIPAA if applicable), full network isolation, ability to run on customer-managed GPUs, isolated cost accounting.
Signals that indicate fit: regulatory requirements, legal/compliance request for data-at-rest and in-network control, very large inference volumes where customer prefers owning infra.
Technical prerequisites: network design (vpc peering, CIDR ranges), KMS/HSM expectations, access model for support (jump host, Bastion protocol), acceptable OS/kernel versions for on-prem agent, air-gap constraints or install windows.
Commercial & legal asks: support SLAs, change window expectations, invoice cadence, licensing model (per-seat vs per-node vs capacity unit).
Common blocker: internal security doesn’t allow external management plane access — propose hybrid private with customer-managed control plane for phased approach.

Premium SLA add-ons (latency/uptime/backups) — value props and checklist
Value props: financially-backed uptime, lower latency SLOs during business hours, formal incident response times, extended data retention for observability.
When to recommend: account sees critical end-user impact from latency or requires contractual uptime.
SLA definition items: uptime %, latency p99 target, scheduled maintenance windows, incident severity matrix + response times, credit calculation formula.
Execution checklist: align SRE/infra team on ops playbook, confirm monitoring hooks (tracing, span sampling), confirm escalation path and paging roster.

4) Common objections & soundbites (short ready replies)
- "We don’t want to commit capital / preferring pay-as-you-go": "Understood — for customers with spiky usage we recommend a hybrid: small Dedicated baseline for peak predictability plus Hosted burst. The modeled TCO shows baseline saves you X% for predictable windows."
- "Security won’t allow external control plane": "We have a Private architecture where the control plane can be customer-managed or a limited control interface for support. I can set up a call with our security architect to walk through network and key management specifics."
- "We don’t have time for migration": "We provide a canary migration path and a dedicated solutions engineer for onboarding. Typical migration for similar customers took 4–8 weeks with zero production downtime during cutover."

5) Tactical outreach cadences (adapt to deal size)
Small expansion (<$30k potential): Email -> 7-day wait -> product walkthrough -> proposal email -> 1-week follow-ups (3 attempts)
Medium ($30k–200k): Personalized email + 3-min Loom -> schedule 30-min review -> technical working session -> TCO proposal -> exec sync -> propose term
Large (>$200k): Exec sponsor intro -> 1:1 with VP-level champion -> dedicated discovery workshop (on-site or virtual) -> security/legal kickoff -> commercial proposal -> contract negotiation

6) Internal playbook — stakeholders & RACI (one-liners)
- CSA: drive QBR, own commercial narrative and relationship management.
- Solutions Engineer: technical discovery, migration planning, canary design.
- Account Exec: commercial terms, pricing, discounts, contract signature.
- Product/SRE: define SLA feasibility and monitoring hooks.
- Legal: contract language and indemnity.
- Finance: approve discounting and billing model.

7) Proposal skeletons (copy/paste snippets)
Executive summary: "Proposal to move {{ACCOUNT_NAME}} to Redwood Dedicated capacity to reduce monthly inference variance, lower unit costs, and guarantee capacity for planned product launches."
Commercial terms (example): "12-month committed Dedicated capacity: 8 vGPU-equivalent units. Monthly commit: $XX,XXX. Burst policy: additional capacity billed at committed rate * 1.5. SLA: 99.95% uptime for serving layer during region business hours."
Technical appendix: include migration plan, rollback plan, smoke test checklist, and monitoring dashboard links.

8) Quick templates (short)
Intro email for proposal: "Hi {{CHAMPION_NAME}}, thanks again for the time. Based on our QBR discussion I’ve attached a short proposal to move to Dedicated capacity that targets a ~Y% reduction in per-token costs and guarantees capacity during peak. Would you like a 30-minute session to walk through the migration plan?"
Security intro to SRE/arch: "Hi security team — Maya from Redwood. We propose a private deployment option for {{ACCOUNT_NAME}}. Attached: network diagram, KMS integration notes, support access model. Can we schedule a 60-min design call?"

9) Post-QBR next-steps checklist (within 48 hours)
- Send meeting notes and decision recap.
- Attach TCO model and proposed contract stub.
- Create Jira ticket for Solutions Eng with required migration tasks and owners.
- Schedule technical validation call (if requested).

10) Open questions & TODOs (for team review)
- Add sample TCO model per region (US-West vs EU) into repo.
- Standardize Dedicated burst pricing formula for proposals.
- Create a one-page security brief for Private deployments (customer-facing).

Notes to self
- Favor granular metrics in QBRs — product leaders respond to curves not single numbers.
- When in doubt, escalate to Solutions Eng early for feasibility.
- Record anonymous win/loss notes in JIRA to refine objection handling.

Revision history
- 2024-10-05 Maya Chen initial draft
- 2024-11-22 Andre Gomez added objection responses and SLA checklist
